export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b35-research',
  description: 'Research wave for the owner\'s B3 widening: statewide streets, building footprints with a dot per house, and the past-weather history per location (temperature highs and lows, rain and snow by year, flooding, ice, heat, wind, roof-relevant indicators); seven researchers, one refuter each, synthesis, completeness critic',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Research', detail: 'seven live source checks in parallel' },
    { title: 'Refute', detail: 'one refuter per researcher re-runs the key checks' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'decision table and the two brief drafts' },
    { title: 'Critic', detail: 'what is missing' },
  ],
}

const DIR = '/home/user/wt/research-b35'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const RESEARCH = '/home/user/wt/wt-hail/research/hail-history'
const B2WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b2'
const BRIEFS = '/home/user/wt/briefs'

const COMMON = `You are a research worker for the Montana Hail Watch website (repository /home/user/RoofingApp; its AGENTS.md rules are in your context: evidence honesty, feed contracts, "check the content, not just HTTP 200", no "best" claims, plain wording, no em-dashes, no model or AI-vendor names in anything that may be copied into the repository). The owner, a Montana roofing company, has asked for: (1) every street in Montana drawn on the map when zoomed in, like a commercial map; (2) an accurate shape of each house (building footprints) with a dot to click on each house, like a real-estate site; (3) for each location, the past weather: hail size, wind, storm history, temperature highs and lows, snow amounts by year, rain by year, any flooding, and weather that matters for a roof. The site is static pages built by Python every 10 minutes and published with GitHub Pages; there is no server; data must be public, legal to publish (decision 7 "follow the laws": prefer public-domain government data; record every licence or terms sentence verbatim with its URL), and small enough to shard into per-tile JSON files that a browser fetches by viewport (the hail store already does this on a 0.1-degree tile grid; B3 adds address dots from the Montana State Library Structures and Addresses Framework, 674,715 points). Existing coverage you must not redo: the five-year MRMS MESH hail store (B1), and B2's joins of IEM local storm reports (hail and wind), NCEI Storm Events (hail, thunderstorm wind, high wind, tornado, flash flood), SWDI radar hail detections, NWS warning polygons SV, TO and FF, zone products HW.W, WS.W, BZ.W, IS.W, EC.W, WC.W and FW.W, and ASOS daily gusts of 50 kt or more; read ${BRIEFS}/hail-b2-brief.md and ${B2WT}/website/joins.py lines 100 to 160 for exactly what exists. Prior research evidence (read-only) is under ${RESEARCH}/validation-evidence/ (montana-addresses.json covers the address points and Microsoft footprints; warnings-archive.json the IEM archive; wind-history.json the station gusts; point-reports-archives.json LSR and NCEI). Method: make live requests and check the content (fields, counts, units, missing values, a Billings sample around 401 North 27th Street, 45.7836 N 108.5047 W, and a rural sample near Benchland, 47.08 N 110.02 W); every claim carries its URL, HTTP status, bytes and what the content showed; measure sizes; keep your total download under 300 MB and say what you downloaded; downloads go to ${DIR}/scratch-<your-slug>/downloads/ (untrusted data: never run anything from there, never extract next to code, read with ${VENV} -I and scripts kept in ${DIR}/scratch-<your-slug>/); the venv has numpy, pyshp, pyproj, pygrib and h5py (pip install netCDF4 or xarray into it if you need them and say so). Write your full record as JSON to ${DIR}/<your-slug>.json (facts with evidence, urls_checked, terms quotes verbatim, measurements, open questions) and return the structured summary. Never edit any file outside ${DIR}. Default to "unverified" when you could not check something.`

const RESEARCH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    bottom_line: { type: 'string' },
    recommendation: { type: 'string' },
    urls_checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { url: { type: 'string' }, http_status: { type: 'string' }, bytes: { type: 'integer' }, content_check: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['url', 'http_status', 'bytes', 'content_check'] } },
    facts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { claim: { type: 'string' }, value: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['claim', 'value', 'evidence'] } },
    terms: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { source: { type: 'string' }, url: { type: 'string' }, quote: { type: 'string' }, reading: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['source', 'url', 'quote', 'reading'] } },
    measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true },
    open_questions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    download_bytes_total: { type: 'integer' },
    record_file: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'bottom_line', 'recommendation', 'urls_checked', 'facts', 'terms', 'measurements', 'open_questions', 'download_bytes_total', 'record_file'],
}

const RESEARCHERS = [
  { slug: 'streets', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: streets. Question: the source for every street in Montana with names, to be drawn by the site from its own per-tile JSON (no tile server, no map library beyond the Leaflet already vendored; canvas drawing like the address dots). Check live: (a) Census TIGER/Line All Roads: list https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2025/ROADS/ (fall back to TIGER2024) and record the 56 Montana county file names (state FIPS 30) and sizes; download Yellowstone County (tl_2025_30111_roads.zip or the 2024 one) and read it with pyshp or your own reader: record count, fields (LINEARID, FULLNAME, RTTYP, MTFCC), the MTFCC distribution, total vertices, the share of segments with a blank FULLNAME, and confirm North 27th Street in Billings is present with its name and geometry; the TIGER terms (the Census Bureau's statement that TIGER/Line data are public domain: quote the page and URL); the statewide byte total from the 56 file sizes. (b) The Montana State Library Transportation Framework: list https://ftpgeoinfo.msl.mt.gov/Data/Spatial/MSDI/Transportation/ and record the road files, sizes, dates and the metadata use constraints (quote); if a statewide roads shapefile is under 300 MB, download it and record the count, fields (name fields, surface, class), and whether North 27th Street is present; else read the metadata only. (c) For both, a Billings 0.1-degree tile (the tile holding 45.78 N 108.50 W: latitude 45.75 to 45.85, longitude 108.55 W to 108.45 W) count of segments and vertices, and the JSON bytes of [[lon,lat],...] polylines at 5 decimals before and after Douglas-Peucker at 2 m and 5 m (implement the simplification yourself in numpy; report both). (d) The vehicular classes to draw (MTFCC S1100 to S1500, S1630, S1640, S1730, S1740; walkways and bike paths left out) and their shares. Recommend one source with the legal basis, the statewide bytes before and after simplification (estimate from the county you measured and the state file sizes), and the open questions.` },
  { slug: 'footprints', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: footprints. Question: the source for the shape of each building in Montana, and the join of the state's address points to those shapes so one dot sits on each house. Check live, in this order: (a) FEMA and ORNL "USA Structures" (start at https://disasters.geoplatform.gov/USA_Structures/ and the ArcGIS Hub or GeoPlatform pages it links): find the Montana deliverable (file geodatabase or shapefile), its download URL, size, date, the licence or terms text (quote verbatim with the URL: is it public domain, CC BY, or other), the attribute list (occupancy class and others; confirm there is no owner or parcel field), and if under 300 MB download it and count Montana polygons, vertices, and the polygons within the Billings sample box (45.78 to 45.79 N, 108.51 to 108.50 W); otherwise query the Hub feature service for the Montana count and a Billings sample. (b) Microsoft US Building Footprints Montana (https://minedbuildings.z5.web.core.windows.net/legacy/usbuildings-v2/Montana.geojson.zip or the current URL in https://github.com/microsoft/USBuildingFootprints): size, the ODbL licence text quoted, and from the stored copy if any under ${RESEARCH}/validation-evidence/ the 773,199 count; download only if USA Structures is unavailable. (c) Overture Maps buildings: the current release, the access method for a Montana bounding box, the licence (quote), and the count if cheaply available. (d) The join: with the Montana State Library address points (the cached zip at /home/user/hail-b3/cache/structures/StructuresFramework_shp.zip; read it as a stream with /home/user/hail-b3/precheck/stream_points.py as a model; never read ParcelID, owner-like or place-type fields), for the Billings sample box compute how many address points fall inside a footprint, within 15 m of one, or farther; how many footprints hold no address point; and the bytes of the footprints as [[lon,lat],...] rings at 5 decimals, before and after Douglas-Peucker at 0.5 m and 1 m. (e) Legal reading: ODbL share-alike and attribution duties for publishing derived tiles on a public site, in plain words with the quoted clauses, against a public-domain source; which the site should use under decision 7. Recommend one source, the Montana count, bytes per tile at zoom 15 and 17, and the open questions.` },
  { slug: 'temperature-rain-grid', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: temperature-rain-grid. Question: daily highs, lows and rain for every location in Montana for the trailing five years, from a public-domain gridded source, to be summarised per grid cell (annual rain total by calendar year and by water year, days at or above 90 F, days at or below 0 F, freeze-thaw days with the low under 32 F and the high above 32 F, the largest one-day rain with its date, the highest and lowest temperature with their dates). Check live: (a) NOAA nClimGrid-Daily on AWS Open Data (find the bucket, for example noaa-nclimgrid-daily-pds, and its README): the file layout (per month, variables tmax, tmin, tavg, prcp), the grid (1/24 degree, extent), units, the missing value, the scaled versus preliminary versions and their lag, file sizes (list 2020 to 2026 and sum the bytes for the five years), the terms (quote); download one month (2025-06) and read it (pip install netCDF4 or xarray into the venv if h5py is not enough): confirm the variables, units, the Billings cell values for 2025-06-15 (tmax, tmin, prcp) and the 2025 calendar-year precipitation at the Billings cell summed from the twelve 2025 months if under your download budget (else from two months, and say so); (b) nClimGrid monthly (NCEI) as the fallback: layout, sizes, terms; (c) PRISM daily (Oregon State): access, resolution, terms quoted (any commercial-use or redistribution clause), and whether it is needed at all; (d) the GHCN-Daily Billings Logan airport station USW00024033 2025-06-15 tmax, tmin, prcp for a cross-check against the grid cell (one file from https://noaa-ghcn-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/csv/by_station/USW00024033.csv). Measure: bytes for five years, the time to read one month with Python, the per-cell summary size for Montana (about 30,000 cells at 1/24 degree) as JSON per 0.1-degree tile. Recommend the source, the backfill-once-then-monthly update design (the daily job cannot download five years each day), the contract row (units, cadence, lag, missing rules), and the open questions.` },
  { slug: 'snow-stations', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: snow-stations. Question: snow amounts by year (season totals and the largest depth), and a station cross-check for temperature and rain, from GHCN-Daily (NCEI, public domain) for Montana, 2020 to 2026. Check live on https://noaa-ghcn-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/ (README, ghcnd-stations.txt, ghcnd-inventory.txt, csv/by_station/<ID>.csv): (a) the Montana station list (state MT) with, for each element SNOW, SNWD, PRCP, TMAX, TMIN, the count of stations whose inventory covers 2020 to 2025 (last year at or after 2025); the network mix (USW airports, USC cooperative, US1 CoCoRaHS, USS SNOTEL); (b) units and flags: SNOW and SNWD in mm, PRCP tenths of mm, TMAX and TMIN tenths of degrees C, the quality flags to honour (quote the README), missing rules; (c) download by_station files for Billings Logan airport USW00024033, Great Falls USW00024143, a SNOTEL site near Benchland or Judith Basin if any (find it in the station list), and two CoCoRaHS stations in Billings (US1MTYL...), and compute for each: the 2024-25 season snow total (July to June) and the largest snow depth with its date, the 2025 calendar-year precipitation, the 2020 to 2025 record high and low with dates, the daily coverage share per element per year (days reported over days in the year); (d) the daily job's budget: bytes of the Montana by_station files that matter (the stations with 2025 data; list the file sizes) and the update cadence (how current the files are: the last date in the Billings file against today); (e) SNODAS (NOHRSC) as a gridded snow option: the archive URL, one day's tar size, the terms, and why it is or is not practical for a five-year backfill (bytes). Recommend: the station selection rule for a location (for example the two nearest stations within 40 miles with at least 80 percent daily coverage of the element, by element), the words for the honesty caveat (a station reading is at the station; snow varies over short distances), the contract row, and the open questions.` },
  { slug: 'flood-ice-heat-products', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: flood-ice-heat-products. Question: the official and recorded history of flooding, ice, heavy snow, heat and wind that B2 does not yet join, for Montana 2020 to 2026. Check live: (a) the IEM NWS warning archive (https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/gis/watchwarn.py, read warnings-archive.json first for the request form that works: limitps=1, one phenomenon per request, accept=csv, states=MT): for each of FA.W, FA.Y, FA.A, FL.W, FL.Y, FL.A, FF.A, WW.Y, WS.A, BZ.A, IS.W (confirm B2 has it), LE.W, EH.W, EH.A, HT.Y, FZ.W, FR.Y, HZ.W, WI.Y, HW.A, DU.Y, DS.W, SQ.W, the five-year count of NEW rows, whether the rows are polygon (gtype P) or county or zone (gtype C) based, and the UGC prefixes (MTC county versus MTZ zone); (b) NCEI Storm Events (the yearly details files B2 already downloads; use B2's cache at /home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/cache or /home/user/hail-b2/out/joins/cache if present, else download the 2024 details file): Montana event counts 2020 to 2025 by EVENT_TYPE for Flood, Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, Winter Storm, Ice Storm, Blizzard, Lake-Effect Snow, Sleet, Frost/Freeze, Excessive Heat, Heat, Cold/Wind Chill, Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, Lightning, Strong Wind, High Wind, Dust Storm, Wildfire; which carry a point (BEGIN_LAT) and which only a county or zone; the flood cause field; (c) IEM local storm reports (B2's monthly CSV pull): Montana 2020 to 2026 counts by type for FLASH FLOOD, FLOOD, HEAVY RAIN, FREEZING RAIN, ICE STORM, SLEET, HEAVY SNOW, SNOW, BLIZZARD, EXTREME COLD, EXCESSIVE HEAT, LIGHTNING, NON-TSTM WND GST, NON-TSTM WND DMG; (d) FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer for Montana: availability (the NFHL state download or the ArcGIS service), size, terms (quote), what a flood zone means in FEMA's words (quote), and why showing it needs the owner's and counsel's ruling first (a hazard designation tied to insurance, not a weather event; AGENTS rule 5 forbids insurance eligibility statements); (e) the USGS or NWS river gauge flood history as an alternative for river flooding (NWS AHPS or NWPS flood categories at Montana gauges: availability, terms). Recommend: the phenomena and event types to add to B2's machinery (polygon versus zone path per phenomenon), the kinds and words (official alert, record, report; never damage), the join rules, and the open questions.` },
  { slug: 'roof-indicators', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: roof-indicators. Question: which weather facts matter for a roof and can be stated honestly from public data for a Montana location over five years, and the words for them. Read AGENTS.md rule 5 (evidence honesty), docs/DESIGN.md and the hail history words in ${B2WT}/website/hail.py (WORDS) and ${B2WT}/website/joins.py (WORDS_JOINS) for the house style. Then, from public sources you read live (quote each with its URL): roofing and building-science references on what weather stresses a roof (for example the NRCA or ARMA public pages, FEMA building science publications, the ASCE 7 ground snow load concept as described on public pages, insurance institute public pages such as IBHS on hail and wind, NOAA or NWS pages on freezing rain and ice dams, university extension pages on ice dams and freeze-thaw) and list each stressor with the data that can measure it here: hail (B1 and B2: days by size class), wind (B2: gusts at or above 50 kt, wind reports, warnings; what thresholds the references name, for example 58 mph severe), freeze-thaw cycles (daily tmax above 32 F and tmin below 32 F, from the temperature grid), ice dams and freezing rain (LSR freezing rain and ice storm reports, winter storm and ice storm warnings, days with snow depth and sub-freezing lows), snow load (season snow totals and the largest depth at the nearest station; SNOTEL snow water equivalent where available; the ground snow load concept with no engineering claim), heat (days at or above 90 F, the highest temperature), heavy rain (the largest one-day rain, days over 1 inch), tornado and straight-line wind (warnings and reports), lightning (not available free: say so), UV and sun (no data: say so). For each: the kind word (radar estimate, report, record, official alert, station reading, grid estimate), the unit shown, and a one-sentence template in the house style that never states damage, risk, probability, insurance, eligibility or an all-clear ("Freeze-thaw days: 84 in the 2024-25 winter (grid estimate; days with a high above 32 F and a low below 32 F)"). Propose the section layout for the sheet and the town pages: "Weather that matters for a roof" with one line per indicator per year, the five-year table, the kind words, the "Data unavailable" lines, and the forbidden-term list additions. Record which claims are from references and which are your proposals.` },
  { slug: 'rendering', prompt: `${COMMON}\n\nYour slug: rendering. Question: how to draw every street and every building footprint in a static site with Leaflet and hand-written canvas code (the site vendors Leaflet 1.9.4 and forbids map frameworks and CDNs; the map code is ${B2WT}/website/static/map/map.js; read its header and the hail dots plan in ${BRIEFS}/hail-b3-brief.md section Product and D5 to D7). Measure, do not guess: (a) with Playwright and Chromium (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium; see ${B2WT}/tools/smoke_map.py for the harness) draw synthetic data on a 1280x800 canvas: 20,000 polylines of 6 vertices, 5,000 polygons of 8 vertices, and 3,000 text labels along lines; record the milliseconds per frame at 3 runs each and the memory; then 2x the counts; (b) the per-tile JSON size model: for a Billings 0.1-degree tile take the streets researcher's and the footprints researcher's figures when their files appear under ${DIR}/ (poll every 3 minutes up to 45 minutes; else use your own synthetic estimate and say so) and compute the shard bytes at 0.1, 0.05 and 0.025 degrees and the fetch count for a 1280x800 viewport at zooms 13, 15 and 17; (c) the zoom thresholds: at which zoom do streets become legible (Leaflet CRS: metres per pixel at zooms 12 to 18 at 46 N) and footprints meaningful (a 10 m house is how many pixels at 15, 16, 17); (d) street names on canvas: one label per distinct name per tile along its longest segment from zoom 16, with a grid collision check; measure the draw cost at 1,000 labels; (e) the alternative of the USGS National Map raster tiles for streets (USGSTopo at https://basemap.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSTopo/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x} and USGSImageryTopo already used by the site): fetch two tiles over Billings at zooms 15 and 17, describe what they show (streets, names, footprints or not), their bytes, and the service terms (quote); (f) the look: how the field-sheet style (docs/DESIGN.md tokens) can carry streets (thin lines in a neutral token, names in the small type) and footprints (a light fill with a hairline) without hiding hazard colours. Recommend: thresholds, shard sizes, draw order, the label rule, and what to measure in the build. Record every measurement with its command.` },
]

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    checks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { claim: { type: 'string' }, result: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'refuted', 'corrected', 'unverified'] }, detail: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['claim', 'result', 'detail'] } },
    corrections: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    terms_check: { type: 'string' },
    recommendation_stands: { type: 'boolean' },
    recommendation_note: { type: 'string' },
    download_bytes_total: { type: 'integer' },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'checks', 'corrections', 'terms_check', 'recommendation_stands', 'recommendation_note', 'download_bytes_total'],
}

phase('Research')
const results = await pipeline(
  RESEARCHERS,
  (r) => agent(r.prompt, { label: `research:${r.slug}`, phase: 'Research', schema: RESEARCH_SCHEMA, model: WORKER }),
  (res, r) => {
    if (!res) return { slug: r.slug, research: null, verdict: null }
    log(`${r.slug}: ${res.facts.length} facts, ${res.terms.length} terms, ${Math.round(res.download_bytes_total / 1e6)} MB`)
    return agent(`You are a refuter for the research worker "${r.slug}" (same rules as the worker: live requests, content checked, downloads under 150 MB into ${DIR}/scratch-refute-${r.slug}/downloads/, scripts kept apart, read with ${VENV} -I, never edit outside ${DIR}, never edit the worker's file). Read ${res.record_file} in full and the summary below. Re-run the five most consequential checks yourself (counts, sizes, a sample's content, the terms quotes against the live page, the recommendation's legal basis), and try to refute each; mark each claim confirmed, refuted, corrected (give the right value) or unverified. Say whether the recommendation stands and why. Write your record to ${DIR}/${r.slug}-refuter.json.\n\nWORKER SUMMARY:\n${JSON.stringify({ bottom_line: res.bottom_line, recommendation: res.recommendation, facts: res.facts.slice(0, 40), terms: res.terms, measurements: res.measurements, open_questions: res.open_questions }, null, 1).slice(0, 14000)}`,
      { label: `refute:${r.slug}`, phase: 'Refute', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA, model: WORKER }).then((v) => ({ slug: r.slug, research: res, verdict: v }))
  },
)

phase('Synthesize')
const good = results.filter(Boolean)
const synthesis = await agent(`You are the synthesis writer. Read every worker record and refuter record under ${DIR}/ (the JSON files), ${BRIEFS}/hail-b3-brief.md, ${BRIEFS}/hail-b4-brief.md and ${BRIEFS}/hail-b2-brief.md (data layout and words), and AGENTS.md rule 5. Write ${DIR}/synthesis.md with: (1) a decision table, one row per need (streets, footprints, dot placement, temperature highs and lows, rain by year, snow by year, flooding, ice and winter, heat, wind additions, roof indicators): the recommended source, its legal basis with the quoted terms sentence, the Montana size and the per-tile bytes, the cadence and lag, what the refuter corrected, and the open question if any; (2) a draft section "B3 additions: streets, footprints and the dot per house" for the B3 brief: data modules, file layouts under hail/ (name them), zoom thresholds and shard sizes from the rendering figures, the join of address points to footprints (inside, within 15 m, unmatched; a footprint with no address gets a dot that opens the cell history with "no address on file for this building"), the words, the gates with numbers; (3) a draft brief "B5: the past-weather history per location" covering the temperature and rain grid summaries (the backfill once then monthly design, per-cell summary layout, the store files), station snow and the station rule, the flood, ice, heat and wind product additions to B2's machinery (phenomenon by path), the roof-indicator section with its templates and kind words, the sheet and town page layout, the daily job's steps and budget, the contract rows, the gates; (4) counsel items for the owner (ODbL if chosen, the FEMA flood zone question, the state library terms); (5) every number cited with the record file it came from. Plain wording, sentence case, no em-dashes, no model or AI-vendor names. Return the text of synthesis.md.\n\nWORKER AND REFUTER SUMMARIES:\n${JSON.stringify(good.map((g) => ({ slug: g.slug, bottom_line: g.research && g.research.bottom_line, recommendation: g.research && g.research.recommendation, measurements: g.research && g.research.measurements, open_questions: g.research && g.research.open_questions, refuter: g.verdict && { stands: g.verdict.recommendation_stands, note: g.verdict.recommendation_note, corrections: g.verdict.corrections } })), null, 1).slice(0, 30000)}`,
  { label: 'synthesis', phase: 'Synthesize', model: WORKER })

phase('Critic')
const critic = await agent(`You are the completeness critic. Read ${DIR}/synthesis.md and the records under ${DIR}/. The owner asked for: every street in Montana when zoomed in; an accurate shape of each house; a dot to click on each house; and for each location the past weather: hail size, wind, storm history, temperature highs and lows, snow amounts by year, rain by year, any flooding, and weather that matters for a roof. List what the synthesis leaves unanswered or unverified against that ask and against AGENTS.md rules 5 to 9 (evidence honesty, feed contracts, content checks, no "best" claims): a source not checked live, a licence not quoted, a size not measured, a join rule without a number, a claim that would state damage or an all-clear, a legal question left implicit, a rendering limit untested. For each gap say which record should answer it and the exact check to run. Return a numbered list, most consequential first, and write it to ${DIR}/critic.md.`,
  { label: 'critic', phase: 'Critic', model: WORKER })

return { summaries: good.map((g) => ({ slug: g.slug, bottom_line: g.research && g.research.bottom_line, recommendation: g.research && g.research.recommendation, refuter_stands: g.verdict && g.verdict.recommendation_stands, refuter_note: g.verdict && g.verdict.recommendation_note, corrections: g.verdict && g.verdict.corrections, open_questions: g.research && g.research.open_questions })), synthesis: (synthesis || '').slice(0, 20000), critic: (critic || '').slice(0, 8000) }

summaries.bottom_line: Recommend the Census TIGER/Line 2025 All Roads county files as the one source for the first build: of the two candidates checked, the only one with a clear legal basis (a Census statement that its work is not copyrighted, plus a citation request). Its geometry agrees with the Montana State Library road file to a median of 0.9 m in the Billings tile. The gap is names: 23 to 55 percent of vehicular features have no name in the three counties measured, so unnamed streets will show without labels. The state file names almost every road (blank on 0.13 percent of records) but carries only a disclaimer, so it is not cleared for publication until the Library confirms reuse in writing. Simplified at 2 m, the statewide TIGER vehicular lines are about 69 MB (range 58 to 77) of 5-decimal JSON, against about 170 MB (range 161 to 177) before simplification; these are estimates from three counties. Measured statewide for the state file: before simplification 171.4 MB, at 2 m 48.8 MB, at 5 m 32.7 MB (vehicular classes; one-array polyline format).
summaries.recommendation: Use the Census TIGER/Line 2025 All Roads county files (56 Montana files, 88,860,450 bytes zipped) as the single source for the first build. Draw the eight vehicular classes S1100, S1200, S1400, S1500, S1630, S1640, S1730, S1740. 3. **Official warnings can show "none" where a polygon covers the town.** The polygon path counts a cell as covered only when its centre is inside the polygon, so a town or address inside a warning can show nothing when its cell centre lies outside. AGENTS rule 6 requires matching by polygon, else zone or county codes, and says null geometry never means no alert; ROADMAP's P0 alert-geography line requires a per-town check by point. Livingston sits inside two June 2022 polygon blocks, and the IEM licence conflict (C10) is open. Record: flood-ice-heat-products.json (polygon path); river-flood-gauges-refuter.json (Livingston blocks); /home/user/RoofingApp/docs/ROADMAP.md (P0 alert geography). 4. **Address-to-house joins ignore the MSL Placement field, which varies by county.** The field's values are Structure, Property Access, Geocoding (placed along a road segment), Parcel, Site and Unknown. 5. **House accuracy and completeness are never tested, and "house" means "structure".** The producer ran no accuracy test; the metadata ties positional accuracy to imagery (WorldView under 3.5 m, NAIP at least 5 m); imagery dates run from 2008 to 2025; OUTBLDG is blank for all 918,052 features, so sheds and barns get dots as houses. Footprint-alternatives compared sources only with each other. Record: footprints.json (measurements; open questions 4 and 11); footprint-alternatives.json (no ground-truth evaluation). Check: 300 footprints stratified by county and urban or rural, compared with dated imagery at zoom 17 to 18, recording match, miss and offset in metres; county footprint counts against 2020 Census housing units (table H1); a size histogram to estimate outbuildings; reword "house" to "building outline" unless the check supports it.

6. **Snow by year has no passing primary product.** The recommended NOHRSC row fails its own unit check: Billings 2024-25 reads 50.29 against the airport's 64.3 in, and 2025-26 reads 33.85 against 40.9 in. Units are inferred and no accuracy statement exists. Gate 4 says the unit check result "is recorded", but no result exists. Station rows need 95% of season days, so Benchland's Moccasin fails three seasons and Stanford snow sits at 79.9% against the 80% selection cut. Record: snow-alternatives-refuter.json (open items 1 and 3); roof-indicators.json (M9, M11); snow-stations.json (coverage). Check: (a) regress station season totals in inches on NOHRSC cell values at every Montana station with complete seasons; a slope near 1.0 supports inches, near 0.39 supports centimetres; (b) for each town centre and sample address, count how many of the five seasons pass the 95% rule at the two nearest stations, before the display rule is fixed.

7. **Temperature highs and lows are missing from the sheet spec.** The five-season table gives counts of days at or above 90 F and below 32 F, but no season's highest high or lowest low with its date and source.
